brief: 8 mistakes I made as a first-time founder that cost me $250K.

slots.title: 1. Hiring, the silent killer
slots.body: I built a six-person team before validating a single dollar of demand. Salaries consumed eighteen months of runway in under nine. Validate first.

slots.title: 2. Burn, the ignored math
slots.body: I spent forty thousand on ads without calculating CAC or LTV. Top-line growth masked the fact that we lost money on every sale.

slots.title: 3. Code, the vanity trap
slots.body: We spent six months perfecting features no user asked for. Launch delays killed momentum and wasted developer hours we could never recover. Ship lean.

slots.title: 4. Ego, the blindfold
slots.body: I skipped customer calls, assuming I understood the pain points. At launch, the product solved problems our target market did not actually have.

slots.title: 5. Books, the unread signal
slots.body: I commingled accounts and ignored monthly burn. By the time I reviewed the books, eighty thousand had vanished into untracked tools and subscriptions.

slots.title: 6. Scope, the focus killer
slots.body: I chased three verticals at once for quick revenue. Each pilot demanded custom work that diluted our roadmap until we served no one well.

slots.headline: Avoid My $250K Mistakes
slots.subline: Save this post and audit your startup before you scale. Protect your runway.
